verdict.text:
Track 1 is measurable here, unlike runs with empty gold labels, but only unevenly so. The condition slot carries real support (21 genuinely-missing cases) and zero-shot Opus handles it well: 18 of 21 flagged, precision 0.90, F1 0.88. That is the one slot where a conclusion is warranted, and it is a positive one. Every other slot has support of 1, 2, or 5 — the scope precision of 0.048 and modalVerb F1 of 0.15 are dominated by false positives against a single or double gold-missing case, and should not be read as slot-level performance. They tell you something different and still useful: the model over-flags. Twenty scope slots the humans judged *implied* were emitted as `<MISSING_SCOPE>`, a 0.31 fill rate, when the human convention is to write "For all users" almost reflexively. That is a formatting-convention divergence, not fabrication.

The genuine fabrication signal sits in action: 5 gold-missing cases, only 1 flagged, flag rate 0.20. 592-Signal is the clean example — the source text is "I hate emoji, but this guy requested it", which states no system behaviour at all, and the model produced "must support 'emoji'". 496-Signal does the same, inventing "change the maximum size of MMS" and naming "the System" as actor from a request that only says the feature would be great. 4333-Signal is the worst case: gold marks all five slots missing, and the model filled actor, modalVerb and action from nothing but a bare Android docs URL. Nine silent fills out of 31 missing slots overall is the headline risk number.

Conversion similarity should be read against the ceiling, and the gap is real but modest. Humans reach 0.58 seq_ratio and 0.47 Jaccard with each other; the LLM sits at 0.45 and 0.30. Cosine is nearly at ceiling (0.62 vs 0.66), which says the model captures roughly the right meaning but not the humans' surface phrasing — consistent with the scope-placeholder divergence above. With 89 pairs and standard deviations of 0.24–0.31, the seq_ratio gap is around half a standard deviation; suggestive, not decisive.

Paska's 47% pass rate looks bad but mostly is not a quality signal. Twelve of the 17 smells are "Not requirement", and they fire almost exclusively on outputs where the model correctly emitted placeholders (2943, 1504, 83, 592) — the detector cannot parse a deliberate `<MISSING_*>` marker. That is why pass rate splits 0.74 for llm_complete versus 0.00 for llm_incomplete. The genuinely informative smells are the five substantive ones: coordination ambiguity on 801, incorrect clause order on 695, imprecise verb on 7310, and non-atomic output on 6457 — the last notable because the input set was pre-filtered for atomicity, so the model introduced that.

Most useful next step: make Paska placeholder-aware so pass rate measures conversion quality rather than placeholder presence, then re-run. Second, the action slot is the only place where fabrication is demonstrable, and 5 cases will not settle it — oversample requirements with genuinely absent system responses before comparing zsl to fsl or cot on this dimension. At n=30 on the pre-filtered atomic subset, everything outside the condition slot is directional only.
